candidate.title: Stamp-based brush engine behind the existing stroke interface (per-dab spacing, true hardness curves, directional/image textures)
descriptionSource: feature-analysis.md (untracked internal analyst artifact; used only as the candidate description, not as an approved design)

candidate.scopeSummary: A stroke is rendered as a sequence of dabs placed along the path at a controllable spacing; each dab contributes a coverage profile; all coverage is accumulated into one stroke buffer by union/max and composited once at the stroke opacity; appearance-changing stamp settings are captured per stroke and recorded in the .paka format.

decisions.name: Adopt an existing third-party library as the dab engine
requirements: Licence must be MIT / Apache-2.0 / BSD / ISC, or a permissive dual licence where Paka elects the permissive branch. GPL, AGPL and a mandatory LGPL branch are not acceptable.
The library's copyright notice and licence text must be copied into THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and shipped with the installer.
The library must be pinned in package.json / Cargo.toml, its exact version recorded here, and re-verified on every bump.
For Apache-2.0: retain any upstream NOTICE content and mark modified files (section 4(b)).
decisions.sourceOfferImplications: none for the permissive licences considered; would arise only under the GPL-family sources in strategy C

decisions.name: Copy or adapt code from an existing brush engine
decisions.reason: Copying or adapting GPL-3.0 / GPL-2.0 code makes Paka a derivative work; Paka is MIT, which is not compatible with distributing GPL-derived code in a non-GPL product. Paka would have to be relicensed GPL.
decisions.sourceOfferImplications: GPL-3.0 section 6 requires the complete corresponding source of the derivative work and applies GPL-3.0 to the whole product. This is a licence change, not a source-offer appendix.

sources.evidence: no licence grant exists to request

decisions.note: GIMP and Krita are mixed-licensed at repository level (GPL / LGPL / CC0 parts). The brush engine itself is GPL. A file-by-file licence scan of any specific file would be required before reconsideration - and the brush engines answer GPL.

decisions.name: Port a particular implementation to TypeScript
decisions.reason: A translation of a GPL implementation is a derivative work of it and must be distributed under the same licence. Renaming symbols, changing language, reformatting or rewriting syntax does not change the status of copied implementation.

decisions.name: Clean-room reimplementation from a GPL source's published behaviour
decisions.reason: Behaviour is not copyrightable, so a reimplementation written from a behavioural description is not a derivative work. This is possible but requires a genuine clean-room protocol, and the candidate does not need it.
requirements: A Paka-authored behaviour specification exists (feature-analysis.md section 8 satisfies this for the candidate)
The implementer has not read the GPL source and does not read it during the work
No GPL code, comments, constants, identifier names, structure or test fixtures are reproduced
The decision to consult the GPL source is recorded explicitly by the coordinator before work starts, naming the implementer
decisions.sourceOfferImplications: none, provided the clean-room protocol is genuinely followed; if it is not, the result falls under strategies C and D
decisions.verdictNote: RESTRICTED, and not recommended. Default is not to consult GPL brush-engine sources.

decisions.name: Separate-process integration (shell out to an external painting application)
decisions.reason: Lowest legal risk of the GPL options: Paka ships and links no GPL code. The risks are mostly non-licence risks (external tool terms, output provenance, product shape) plus the fact that the stamp engine is confirmed pure front-end.
requirements: The specific external tool and its specific automation/CLI licence must be checked separately and recorded
That tool's trademark and attribution requirements must be satisfied
The tool's output licence must not be asserted by Paka beyond what the tool and its inputs grant
decisions.sourceOfferImplications: none for Paka; GPL obligations attach to the external program and its users
decisions.architectureNote: Rejected for this slice: docs/SESSION-BRIEF.md section 9 and feature-analysis.md section 7 confirm the stamp engine is pure front-end and the Rust shell is not involved.
